system:
You audit the knowledge atoms of one Knowledge Card. A card is the answer key for a benchmark of expert conceptual knowledge, so every atom must be correct, self-contained, and assessable on its own.

Judge every atom on every check listed below. Rules:
- For checks about evidence, use only the evidence sentences supplied with the atom. Do not repair an atom with your own knowledge.
- For GROUNDED, use "hold" when unreadable PDF symbols prevent verification; explain what is needed. Use fail only when the available evidence is sufficient to determine that the claim is unsupported. This hold rule takes precedence over the strictness rule. Judge other checks independently using their listed values; do not invent missing facts.
- Be strict within each check's allowed values. Do not turn an inability to verify GROUNDED into revise or fail; use hold as defined above.
- "why" is required for every value other than the first listed value; keep it under 30 words. Omit "why" when passing.

Checks (allowed values in brackets; the first value means no problem):
- GROUNDED [pass / revise / fail / hold]: The cited evidence sentences state the atom, including its specificity, causal force, assumptions, and certainty. pass = fully stated. revise = partly stated (the atom adds, drops, or strengthens something; say what). fail = not stated when the available evidence permits a judgment. hold = unreadable symbols prevent verification. For pass or revise, put the supporting evidence ids in cite.
- SINGLE_CLAIM [pass / revise]: The atom is one independently assessable claim. revise = it joins two or more claims that could be true or false separately. Evidence spanning more than three sentences is not by itself a reason to split or revise an atom.
- SCOPE_LABEL [pass / revise]: The S label fits (S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends). revise = wrong label; put the right one in why, e.g. 'S2: ...'.
- L1_ONLY [pass / fail]: The atom is recall-level knowledge. fail = knowing it requires applying the concept to a new problem, or combining facts from distant passages.
- SOURCE_INDEPENDENT [pass / revise / fail]: A domain expert who never read this book could judge the claim true or false. revise = phrased as the authors' statement but the claim itself is general (drop the attribution). fail = an isolated study finding, conjecture, or author-specific opinion, classification, or recommendation, even if attribution was removed. Explicitly scoped established facts about a formalism or architecture and conditional theoretical results remain eligible.
- NO_OVERLAP [pass / fail]: No other atom in this card states or contains the same claim. If two atoms overlap, fail only the less informative one and put the other atom's id in cite; the other one passes.
- CENTRALITY [pass / fail]: The atom matters for understanding the concept. fail = peripheral detail.
Whole-card checks (report under "batch"):
- CONCEPT_SCOPE [pass / fail]: The concept is a general concept of the field. fail = a topic whose assessable content is restricted to excluded study-specific findings or author-specific positions. A named formalism, system, or architecture is not disqualified solely for being specific if its scoped conceptual facts are source-independent.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"units": {"<atom_id>": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": "", "cite": []}, ...}, ...}, "batch": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": ""}}}

CONCEPT: Boardman–Vogt resolution
ASSESSMENT SCOPE: Cover the topological Boardman-Vogt resolution W(P) through labelled metric trees, its quotient relations, grafting composition and augmentation to P, with W(P)-algebras interpreted through coherent homotopies. Include the simplicial analogue using Delta[1] and the explicit free-tree operation-space description on p107; exclude general cofibrancy or weak-equivalence claims and the separate homotopy-coherent nerve construction.

ATOMS:
- MATH-TOP-C03-S1-01 | S1
  ATOM: For an operad P, the Boardman–Vogt resolution is an operad W(P) with the same set of colours as P, equipped with an operad map ε: W(P) → P that is the identity on colours, so that W(P)-algebras are meant to be 'P-algebras up to coherent homotopy'.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0047-s03] For an operad P, we will present a ‘resolution’ by a map of operads
    [MATH-TOP-p0047-s04] ε : W(P) −→P.
    [MATH-TOP-p0047-s05] The new operad W(P) has the same set of colours as P and the map ε is the identity on colours.
    [MATH-TOP-p0047-s09] The idea is that W(P)-algebras are ‘P-algebras up to coherent homotopy’.
- MATH-TOP-C03-S1-02 | S1
  ATOM: Operations of W(P)(c_1,…,c_n; c) are represented by trees labelled as for the free operad FU(P) (edges labelled by colours of P, vertices by operations of P) with each edge additionally given a length t ∈ [0,1], where the external edges (leaves and root) must all have length 1.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0048-s18] For its construction, recall that elements in FU(P)(c1, . . ., cn; c) are represented by trees T with leaves labelled by the set {c1, . . ., cn} and root by c.
    [MATH-TOP-p0048-s19] The edges of T are labelled by colours in C and the vertices of T are labelled by operations of P.
    [MATH-TOP-p0048-s22] The elements of W(P)(c1, . . ., cn; c) are represented by labelled trees as for FU(P), where in addition the edges are all given a length t ∈[0, 1] ⊆R.
    [MATH-TOP-p0048-s23] This assignment of lengths must be such that the external edges of T, i.e. the leaves and the root, all have length 1.
- MATH-TOP-C03-S1-03 | S1
  ATOM: The operad W(P) is a topological operad even when P itself is discrete, and the construction applies to P an operad in sets or in topological spaces.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0047-s10] This operad W(P) will be a topological operad, also when P itself is discrete.
    [MATH-TOP-p0048-s14] It can be an operad in sets or in topological spaces.
- MATH-TOP-C03-S2-01 | S2
  ATOM: The equivalence relation on length-labelled trees representing operations of W(P) is generated by three kinds of identifications: isomorphisms of trees respecting labellings (including lengths), contraction of edges of length zero, and erasure of vertices labelled by a unit operation.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0050-s07] The equivalence relation on such representatives is generated by identiﬁcations of three kinds:
    [MATH-TOP-p0050-s08] (i) one related to isomorphisms of trees, respecting the labellings, (ii) one related to edges of length zero, (iii) one related to vertices labelled by a unit.
- MATH-TOP-C03-S2-02 | S2
  ATOM: Composition in W(P) is defined by grafting: the ith leaf of a tree T is identified with the root of a tree S_i, carrying along all labels, which is possible because these edges share the same colour and the same length 1; hence compositions of subtree operations are recognized by edges of length 1.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0051-s03] The composition operations of the operad W(P) are again deﬁned by grafting, just like for free operads.
    [MATH-TOP-p0051-s06] sends operations represented by trees T, S1, . . ., Sn to the operation represented by identifying the ith leaf of T with the root of Si and carrying along all the labels.
    [MATH-TOP-p0051-s07] Note that this ith leaf has the same colour as the root of Si, as well as the same length (namely 1).
    [MATH-TOP-p0051-s08] Thus, one can recognize operations in W(P) that arise as a composition of operations represented by subtrees by looking for edges of length 1.
- MATH-TOP-C03-S2-03 | S2
  ATOM: In W(P), an edge of length zero may be contracted, with the newly arising vertex labelled by the appropriate composition in P (for example p∘_c r), and a vertex labelled by a unit operation may be erased, with the new edge receiving as length the maximum of the lengths of the two edges adjacent to that vertex.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0049-s04] If an edge has length zero, then the operation in W(P) represented by that labelled tree is to be identiﬁed with the one represented by the smaller labelled tree obtained by contracting the edge of length zero and labelling the newly arising vertex by the appropriate composition in P.
    [MATH-TOP-p0049-s11] The other relation identiﬁes a labelled tree where a vertex v is labelled by a unit operation of P with the smaller labelled tree obtained by ‘erasing’ that vertex and giving the newly arising edge as its length the maximum of the lengths of the two edges connected to v.
    [MATH-TOP-p0050-s03] Here the new length u is the maximum of s and t.
- MATH-TOP-C03-S3-01 | S3
  ATOM: For the free operad Ω(T) on a tree T, the simplicial set WΩ(T)(e_1,...,e_n;e) is empty unless T has a subtree S with leaves e_1,...,e_n and root e, in which case it equals $\prod_{s\in in(S)}\Delta[1]$ over the inner edges of S.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0107-s15] For a sequence e1, . . ., en, e of such edges, the simplicial set WΩ(T)(e1, . . ., en; e) is empty unless there exists a subtree S of T whose leaves are e1, . . ., en and whose root is e.
    [MATH-TOP-p0107-s16] In this case
    [MATH-TOP-p0107-s17] WΩ(T)(e1, . . ., en; e) = Ö ∆[1], s∈in(S)
    [MATH-TOP-p0107-s18] the product now ranging over the inner edges s of S.
- MATH-TOP-C03-S3-02 | S3
  ATOM: The simplicial Boardman–Vogt resolution WP of a simplicial operad P is built analogously to the topological one by replacing the unit interval with the simplex $\Delta[1]$, giving a simplicial operad with a map to P that is the identity on colours.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0107-s03] For a simplicial operad P, one can mimic the topological Boardman–Vogt resolu- tion for topological operads (as in Section 1.7) and construct a simplicial operad WP equipped with a map to P which is the identity on colours.
    [MATH-TOP-p0107-s04] The modiﬁcation to the simplicial case is done completely analogously to the W-construction for simplicial categories of Section 2.7.3, replacing the topological unit interval by the simplex ∆[1].
- MATH-TOP-C03-S3-03 | S3
  ATOM: When the operad P has only unary operations (i.e. is a simplicial category), the simplicial Boardman–Vogt resolution agrees with the W-construction for simplicial categories.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0107-s10] For now, we note that if P has only unary operations (i.e. is a simplicial category), this W-construction agrees with the one given in Section 2.7.3.
- MATH-TOP-C03-S3-04 | S3
  ATOM: When P has only unary operations, so that it is a category, W(P) is a topological category whose morphisms are strings of arrows with waiting times in [0,1], and an algebra over it respects identities but respects composition only up to homotopy, so it is not a functor on the original category.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0051-s18] The operad W(C) has the same colours and again only unary operations.
    [MATH-TOP-p0051-s19] So it is a category with the same objects as C which is enriched in topological spaces; in other words, W(C) is a topological category.
    [MATH-TOP-p0051-s20] For two objects a and b, the space of morphisms W(C)(a, b) can be described as the space of equivalence classes of strings of the form
    [MATH-TOP-p0052-s22] Thus, the At( f2, f1) provide a homotopy between A( f2 f1) and the composition A( f2)◦ A( f1).
    [MATH-TOP-p0052-s23] This shows that A is not a functor on C itself: it respects identities, but it respects composition only up to homotopy.
